b1_base_model: Fine-tuned from our general EN→DE engine v4 (in-house, proprietary licence)
b1_one_line: Faster, more consistent German legal translation for DACH legal and compliance teams
b2_use_cases:
1. Contracts and terms of service
2. Privacy notices and consent text
3. Regulatory filings and internal policies
b2_customers: In-house legal, compliance and procurement teams at EU enterprises, and knowledge teams at law firms
b2_out_of_scope: Court filings, and anything published without human legal review. Swiss and Austrian legal German: use the generic engine.
b3_sources: 1.8M segments: 1.2M licensed EU legal corpus, 450k public EUR-Lex, 150k synthetic back-translation
b3_domains: Contracts, privacy and regulatory text in German (Germany)
b3_cleaning: Near-duplicate removal, PII masking with named-entity detection, length-ratio and QE-score filters
b3_customer_data: None. The shared model contains no customer content.
b4_headline: Legal linguists saved 22 minutes per 1,000 words in a 40k-word pilot
b5_weaknesses: Quality drops on sentences over 60 words, on Swiss and Austrian legal terms, and on deeply nested defined terms. Thin coverage of litigation.
b5_error_modes: Defined terms rendered two ways within one contract (e.g. Vertrag and Vereinbarung for Agreement). Modal verbs softened, e.g. shall translated as sollte instead of muss.
b5_mitigations: The terminology agent enforces defined terms, a negation check flags missing nicht or kein, and every segment is reviewed by a legal linguist.
b6_latency: Median 0.9 s and p95 2.4 s per 1,000 words, measured on one L4 GPU at eight concurrent requests using the Legal DE test set.
b6_throughput: About 400k words per hour per region, measured on four L4 GPUs at steady load.
b6_limits: 512 tokens per segment; documents are split at sentence boundaries
b6_formats: DOCX, XLIFF 1.2 and 2.0, JSON, HTML and plain text
b7_how_used: The machine translation step of the Legal workflow, before APE post-editing and human review
b7_routing_note: Chosen automatically when content is tagged legal and the language pair is EN→DE
b7_cortex: Reads the approved legal glossary and translation memory from Cortex; never writes to it
b7_api: Available through the arbitr API and the Drupal and Zendesk connectors
c1_locales: de-DE only, with formal Sie enforced
c1_domains: Legal: contracts, privacy and regulatory text
c1_terminology: Glossary and do-not-translate lists are enforced by the terminology agent, with 98.6% enforcement on the Legal DE test set.
c1_tm: Exact and fuzzy TM matches from Cortex are reused before MT, adding 6 pts of leverage on legal content.
c1_tags: XLIFF inline tags are preserved; tag error rate 0.3% on the test set
c1_migration: Supports customers moving off ModernMT legal profiles before its December 2026 sunset; TM moves across via Cortex import.
d1_packaging: Add-on to the Pro and Enterprise plans. Billed in Intelligence Credits: 12 credits per 1,000 words (generic engine: 10).
d1_margin: About 71% gross margin at list price, after inference and amortised build cost
d2_signals: More than 1M legal words a year into German; currently on ModernMT or DeepL; regulated industry
d2_disqualifiers: See B2 Out of scope and B5 Known weaknesses and gaps. Also a poor fit under 200k words a year.
d2_questions: How many legal words do you translate into German a year? Who reviews them today? Which engine are you on, and when does it renew?
d2_objections: "DeepL is good enough": run the two-week bake-off and compare minutes saved on their own contracts.
d3_eval_offer: A free two-week bake-off on up to 50k words of the customer's own legal content
d3_success: At least 15 minutes saved per 1,000 words, with no increase in critical MQM errors
d3_onboarding: 1. Signature  2. Connector set-up  3. Glossary import into Cortex  4. First job  5. Joint review of the first 10k words
